prompts.description: Scan the corpus for secrets and PII and summarize findings.
prompts.name: audit_corpus

prompts.description: Summarize a corpus document, treating it as untrusted data.
prompts.name: summarize_document

resource_templates.description: One corpus document, sanitized for its format.

resources.description: The corpus documents the caller is authorized to read.

tools.description:
Evaluate an arithmetic expression with + - * / and parentheses.
Example: calculate(expression="2 * (3 + 4)") returns 14.
tools.name: calculate

tools.description:
Index corpus documents into a pgvector collection so vector_query can
retrieve them. Each document under the path prefix is chunked, embedded, and
written under the caller's tenant; a re-index replaces a document's existing
chunks. Example: doc_index(collection="doc_chunks", path_prefix="handbook/").
tools.name: doc_index

tools.description:
Read a JSON, Markdown, or text document from the corpus by relative
path. Returns sanitized content wrapped with provenance. Example:
doc_read(path="notes/todo.md").
tools.name: doc_read

tools.description:
Retrieve a JSON, Markdown, or text document from a public URL,
SSRF-guarded and sanitized. Returns wrapped, untrusted content.
Example: doc_retrieve(url="https://example.com/data.json").
tools.name: doc_retrieve

tools.description:
Scan corpus documents for secrets and PII and return redacted
findings (type, location, and a hashed placeholder, never the raw
value). Example: doc_scan(path_prefix="exports/").
tools.name: doc_scan

tools.description:
Search corpus documents for a query and return bounded, sanitized
snippets. Literal by default; set use_regex when enabled. Example:
doc_search(query="deadline", path_prefix="notes/").
tools.name: doc_search

tools.description:
Write a JSON, Markdown, or text document to the corpus. Creates a new
document; set overwrite to replace an existing one, which asks for
confirmation. Example: doc_write(path="notes/todo.md", content="# Todo").
tools.name: doc_write

tools.description:
Read a text file from the server's sandbox directory by relative
path. Example: read_file(path="notes/readme.txt").
tools.name: read_file

tools.description:
Fetch a public http or https URL and return its status, content
type, and body text. Private, loopback, link-local, and cloud metadata
addresses are refused. Example: safe_fetch(url="https://example.com/").
tools.name: safe_fetch

tools.description:
Start a background secrets-and-PII scan of the corpus (or a path prefix)
and return a task handle immediately. Poll it with task_get(task_id=...) and
cancel it with task_update(task_id=..., action="cancel"). Example:
scan_corpus_async(path_prefix="exports/").
tools.name: scan_corpus_async

tools.description:
Run a read-only SQL query and return its rows as untrusted data. Only a
single SELECT may run; every referenced table is authorized, and results
are capped. Bind values with named parameters. Example: sql_query(query=
"select id, email from users where org = :org", params={"org": "acme"}).
tools.name: sql_query

tools.description:
Return the status of a task you started, and its result once it has
finished. A task id you do not own is reported as not found. Example:
task_get(task_id="3f2a...").
tools.name: task_get

tools.description:
Update a task you started. The only action is "cancel", which stops a
running task. A task id you do not own is reported as not found. Example:
task_update(task_id="3f2a...", action="cancel").
tools.name: task_update

tools.description:
Find the corpus chunks most similar to a natural-language query, scoped
to the caller's tenant. The query is embedded server-side, only an
allow-listed collection is searched, and each result carries its source
document and chunk index as a citation. Example:
vector_query(collection="doc_chunks", query="how do refunds work?", k=5).
tools.name: vector_query

tools.description:
Find the nearest rows in a pgvector collection to a query embedding,
scoped to the caller's tenant. Only an allow-listed collection may be
searched, the tenant is the caller, and results are capped. Example:
vector_search(collection="documents", embedding=[0.1, 0.2, ...], k=5).
tools.name: vector_search
